title: Landau Theory for Commensurate Charge-Density Waves Coupled to Uniform Lattice Deformation
authors: Keiji Nakatsugawa, Toshiyuki Fujii, Satoshi Tanda
abstract: We formulate a minimal Landau theory for a charge-density wave (CDW) whose commensurability is defined with respect to a deformed lattice. The motivation is provided by recent observations on an isolated single NbS$_3$ chain, which exhibits a commensurate CDW state accompanied by a $6\%$ shrinkage of the lattice constant. A uniform stretch $a_0\to a_0(1+\varepsilon)$ changes the reciprocal lattice wave number to $G(\varepsilon)=G_0/(1+\varepsilon)$, so that an $N$-fold commensurate CDW has the wave number $Q_\mathrm{C}(\varepsilon)=G(\varepsilon)/N$, whereas the wave number $Q_\mathrm{IC}$ favored by the incommensurate instability remains fixed. We propose an amplitude-strain free energy for both $N=3$ and $N=4$, in which the CDW induces a finite uniform strain by relieving the mismatch between $Q_\mathrm{C}(\varepsilon)$ and $Q_\mathrm{IC}$. The mismatch is shared between the CDW and the lattice in a proportion set by their stiffness ratio; since the CDW stiffness grows with the CDW amplitude, the lattice takes up an increasing share of the mismatch as the CDW develops. Our results suggest a reexamination of lock-in theories and of strain-tuning experiments on density-wave systems.
summary: This work formulates a Landau theory for CDWs coupled to a deformable lattice, addressing the limitations of treating the lattice as rigid. It shows that the CDW and lattice share the geometric mismatch proportionally based on their relative stiffnesses. The results provide a unified picture of commensurate lock-in, suggesting that lattice elasticity is a crucial, often overlooked, degree of freedom in density-wave systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a minimal Landau theory to describe Charge-Density Waves (CDWs) whose commensurability is defined relative to a lattice that can undergo uniform deformation.
main_result: The theory successfully interpolates between rigid and soft lattice limits, showing that the lattice strain and CDW amplitude are coupled, leading to a feedback mechanism that stabilizes the commensurate state.
method: The authors minimize the coupled free energy density with respect to the CDW order parameter and the lattice strain, deriving equilibrium conditions based on stiffness ratios.
model_or_system: The model describes a CDW coupled to a lattice strain ($\varepsilon$), motivated by observations in single-chain $	ext{NbS}_3$ where a commensurate CDW is accompanied by lattice shrinkage.
key_observables: Equilibrium lattice strain ($\varepsilon$), CDW amplitude ($\Delta_C$), and the resulting wave number mismatch.
important_parameters: Stiffness ratio ($S = \kappa/\kappa_{CDW}$), geometric misfit ratio ($r = Q_{IC}/Q_{C0}$), and the commensurability number ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a single-mode ansatz for the CDW, excluding discommensurations, and assumes the lattice deformation is uniform.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the strain free energy density dependence on strain ($\epsilon$) for different misfit ratios ($r$) and stiffness ratios ($S$), and show the temperature evolution of CDW amplitude and strain in the soft limit.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the coupled free energy functional, analyzes the limiting cases (rigid vs. soft lattice), derives the equilibrium strain and CDW amplitude, and discusses the implications for existing lock-in theories.
why_interesting: While focused on CDWs, the methodology of coupling an order parameter to a mechanical degree of freedom (strain) and analyzing the resulting phase transition/locking mechanism is highly relevant to understanding coupling effects in quantum many-body systems.
